temperature-chart-nav-desc: Here you can see a daily evolution of the temperature of all the sensors you have in the application
temperature-chart-desc: Here you can see a daily evolution of the temperature of all the sensors you have in the application and chose what date you want to see using the controls
temperature-chart-canvas-desc: Here you can see the evolution of the temperature during the day each sensor specified with the color and name at the bottom, you can also hover over the line or click on the legend at the bottom to hide or show the lines, you can play with this graph right now before moving forward. By default, this chart will display the actual date
temperature-chart-controls-desc: This are the controls to manage what date you will see in the chart
temperature-chart-previous-day-desc: This button moves to the previous day of what is displayed in the middle field
temperature-chart-next-day-desc: This button moves to the next day of what is displayed in the middle field
temperature-chart-date-picker-desc: If you click here you will be able to pick a specific date from a calendar or jump directly to the "Today" date
sensors-nav-desc: Here you can see a list of the sensors in a list displaying the complete information of each for example, last temperature read, battery level, last reading time, etc
sensors-desc: Here you can see a list of the sensors in a list, here you have all the information regarding to the sensor and you can chose to rename the sensor, configure, delete and other options
sensors-table-name-desc: This is the name of the sensor, by default you will have the identifier assigned randomly to the sensor but you can change it whenever you want
sensors-table-battery-desc: In this column you will see the last battery output of the sensor measured in precentage, you can also set it to see the raw reading value
sensors-table-last-reading-desc: This column will show when was the last information sent to the node in combination with the previous column you can know if the sensor has run out of battery or if it just failed to report
sensors-table-temperature-desc: This value represents the latest temperature reading from the sensor in the format you chose in the setup or in the basic settings
sensors-table-signal-desc: This column will show a true or false value deppending on if the sensor was signaling or not, this is useful when you have to reconogize a sensor and the name or the location is wrong
sensors-table-tendency-desc: This column will take the last five readings and calculate a tendency to see if the temperature is rising or descending without the need to check in the temperature chart
sensors-table-actions-desc: These buttons are to do different things with the sensor, for example, renaming it, configuring, deleting, hiding, etc
sensors-table-row-desc: Here you can see an example of what the sensor will look like when its added to the application, the values of temperature might be wrong since its static data
sensors-table-actions-edit-name-desc: Here you can edit the sensor name, you can use the sensors without naming them, but you will see something like "1f96b3ec-a6fb-40a1-97df-8ddc7d99c76c", that is the sensor identifier, but you can rename it with this button
sensors-table-actions-sensor-chart-desc:
**COMMING SOON**
This option will take you to the temperature chart just for this sensor in case you want to see the daily info for the chosen sensor
**COMMING SOON**
sensors-table-actions-hide-desc: If you have a sensor that you want to avoid showing in the table you click in this button and it will hide it just for you, in different devices all the sensors will be visible unless the user decides to hide them
sensors-table-actions-settings-desc: This button will take you to a different page where you can configure specific things about the sensor, the name, light schedule or disabling the light notifications all togheter
sensors-table-actions-delete-desc: This button is to delete a sensor in case that you want to delete all the history belonging to that sensor, this is a destructive action, so be aware that unless you did a backup the information is lost forever
basic-settings-nav-desc: Here you can configure basic things of the application, like timezone, units, etc
advanced-settings-nav-desc: This section is the advanced settings, this section is always password protected, the password is the one you set up during the initial setup
advanced-settings-general-tab-desc: Here you will find the generalistic options on how you can set-up your application
advanced-settings-desc: This section is the advanced settings, this section is always password protected, the password is the one you set up during the initial setup. During the tour the password is disabled but after the tour you will be prompted to login before accesing this screen
advanced-settings-update-section-desc: Here you can chose if you want to check atomatically for the latest versions that option is opt-out, the automatic updates, the ones that update the software are opt-in
advanced-settings-battery-section-desc: This two fields are to calibrate the percentages that you will see in the "Sensors" section, this is because batteries not allways yield the same readings, so you can calibrate them to see the correct percentage in that table
advanced-settings-vesrsion-section-desc: Here you have all the versions of all the parts that compose the application, what whas updated can be checked clicking on the version number. The PCB is not software, is the hardware of the sensor, all the updates to the hardware will be compatible with the sensor software and the pieces of the old PCB
advanced-settings-backup-section-desc: This section is simple, if you want to have a backup of the data or migrate to a different system or clone the one you have you can export all the information in SQL format to be inserted or transformed, the information is yours
advanced-settings-network-tab-desc: Here you can set up the Network Settings of the application
advanced-settings-ap-section-desc: In case you want to change the name of the Access Point of the node or the password you can do it here, any change you do here it will mean that you will have to manually reconfigure the sensors
advanced-settings-security-tab-desc: Here you can change the Admin Password, The SSH password and the Application Security Profile
advanced-settings-system-password-sectio: Here you can change the Admin Password and get the SSH password, the SSH password is generated randomly during installation, if for some reason you need to connect to the SSH you can find the password here
advanced-settings-application-security-s:
Here you have 3 options
Open: all the pages are accesible without prompting for the admin password but this one
Settings: it will only ask password only to access basic settings and advanced settings
All: All pages will be password protected
advanced-settings-users-tab-desc:
**COMMING SOON**

This option is still being developed, the idea is to have different users with different access roles, but again, it still under developement
**COMMING SOON**
advanced-settings-dashboard-tab-desc:
**COMMING SOON**

This option is still being developed, this is the welcome page configuration where you will be able to configure what you see in the home screen of the app
**COMMING SOON**
help-nav-desc: Here you can find specific help of the different sections or even trigger the tour for a specific section if you want to repeat it
